fields.name: Nagata's conjecture on plane curves through very general points
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; linear systems of plane curves
fields.statement: Let $p_1,\dots,p_r$ be very general points of the complex projective plane. Nagata, in his work on Hilbert's fourteenth problem, conjectured that for $r\ge 10$ every nonzero effective plane curve $C$ of degree $d$ with $\mathrm{mult}_{p_i}C\ge m_i$ satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^r m_i < d\sqrt r$. He proved it when $r$ is a perfect square at least $16$. The bound fails at $r=9$ (a cubic through nine points), and partial results (Roé, Harbourne, Ciliberto-Miranda degenerations, the $117/37$ bound at ten points) left every nonsquare $r\ge10$ open. Equivalently, the multipoint Seshadri constant of a line at $r\ge10$ very general points is $1/\sqrt r$. Does the strict inequality $\sum_i m_i<d\sqrt r$ hold for every $r\ge 10$, every degree and every multiplicity vector?

fields.ageNote: Nagata, On the 14-th problem of Hilbert, Amer. J. Math. 81 (1959), cited by the manuscript; see also his Tata lectures (1965).

fields.name: The qualitative Nagata-Biran-Szemberg conjecture: maximal multipoint Seshadri constants for many very general points
fields.field: Algebraic geometry; Seshadri constants and positivity
fields.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ with an ample line bundle $L$, and let $\varepsilon(X,L;p)$ be the multipoint Seshadri constant at $r$ points, the infimum of $L\cdot C/\sum_i\mathrm{mult}_{p_i}C$ over curves $C$. It is always at most $(L^n/r)^{1/n}$. Generalizing Nagata's plane conjecture, and motivated by Biran's symplectic packing stability, Szemberg and coauthors conjectured that on surfaces equality holds at $r$ very general points for every sufficiently large $r$ (Strycharz-Szemberg and Szemberg 2004, in a stronger form with an explicit threshold; Syzdek-Szemberg 2010, Conjecture 4.3), and Roé and Ross stated the same eventual maximality in every dimension over uncountable algebraically closed fields (2009, Conjecture 1.3). Harbourne had it when $rL^2$ is a square. Is there, for every polarized $(X,L)$, a threshold $r_0$ such that $\varepsilon(X,L;p)=(L^n/r)^{1/n}$ at very general $p$ for every $r\ge r_0$?

fields.ageNote: 2004 is the stronger Strycharz-Szemberg-Szemberg conjecture (Serdica Math. J. 30), which contains the qualitative one; the manuscripts cite Syzdek-Szemberg (2010) for the qualitative surface statement and Roé-Ross (2009) for arbitrary dimension. Biran's packing stability (1999) is the symplectic precedent.

fields.name: Are all word-hyperbolic groups residually finite?
fields.statement: A group is residually finite if every nonidentity element survives in some finite quotient. Is every word-hyperbolic group residually finite? The question goes back to Gromov's theory of hyperbolic groups (1987) and is formulated, with its consequences, by Agol, Groves and Manning (2009, Section 5): a positive answer would make every quasiconvex subgroup of every hyperbolic group separable. Kapovich and Wise showed it is equivalent to every nontrivial hyperbolic group having a nontrivial finite quotient, and to every hyperbolic group being virtually torsion-free. Agol's theorem gives residual finiteness for cubulated hyperbolic groups, and non-residually-finite nonpositively curved examples (Wise, Burger-Mozes) were known only outside the hyperbolic class. Is every word-hyperbolic group residually finite?

fields.name: Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the wave equation in three spatial dimensions
fields.field: Harmonic analysis; dispersive and wave equations
fields.statement: For the half-wave propagator $e^{it\sqrt{-\Delta}}$ on $\mathbb R^n$, the sharp fixed-time estimate on $L^p$ loses $(n-1)|1/2-1/p|$ derivatives. Sogge (1991) conjectured that averaging over $t\in[1,2]$ gains almost $1/p$ of a derivative for $p\ge 2n/(n-1)$: $\|e^{it\sqrt{-\Delta}}f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n\times[1,2])}\le C\|f\|_{W^{\sigma,p}}$ for $\sigma>(n-1)(1/2-1/p)-1/p$, and $\sigma>0$ for $2<p\le 2n/(n-1)$. It implies the Bochner-Riesz conjecture and was proved for $n=2$ by Guth, Wang and Zhang (2020). In three spatial dimensions the critical exponent is $p=3$; Bourgain-Demeter decoupling gave the conjecture for $p\ge4$, Gan-He-Li-Wu for $p\ge10/3$, and at $p=3$ only $\sigma>1/12$ was known. Does the estimate hold in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $2<p<\infty$ and every $\sigma>\max\{0,1-3/p\}$, in particular at $p=3$ with every positive loss?
fields.posedBy: Christopher D. Sogge
fields.ageNote: Sogge, Propagation of singularities and maximal functions in the plane, Invent. Math. 104 (1991), Section 4, cited by the manuscript as the source of the higher-dimensional formulation.

The manuscript uses two external published inputs, the planar Furstenberg theorem of Ren-Wang and the cone wave-envelope theorem of Guth-Wang-Zhang.

fields.name: The Borel conjecture for closed aspherical four-manifolds (homeomorphism form)
fields.statement: A connected manifold is aspherical if its universal cover is contractible, so its fundamental group determines its homotopy type. In a letter to Serre of May 2, 1953, Borel asked whether compact manifolds that are classifying spaces for the same group are homeomorphic. The topological Borel conjecture asks, in every dimension, that every homotopy equivalence between closed aspherical manifolds be homotopic to a homeomorphism; the weaker homeomorphism-existence form asks only that homotopy-equivalent closed aspherical manifolds be homeomorphic. It holds in dimensions at most three, and in dimensions at least five for large classes of groups (Farrell-Jones, Bartels-Lück, including hyperbolic and CAT(0) groups). In dimension four it was known only with extra hypotheses such as a good fundamental group in Freedman's sense. Are homotopy-equivalent closed aspherical four-manifolds always homeomorphic?

fields.name: The ionization conjecture: bounded excess charge, ionization energy and radius for Coulomb atoms and molecules (Simon's Problem 9)
fields.statement: For the nonrelativistic Coulomb Hamiltonian of $n$ electrons (two spin states, Fermi statistics) around fixed nuclei of total charge $Z$, let $N_c$ be the largest number of electrons that is strictly bound. Lieb proved $N_c<2Z+M$, Lieb-Sigal-Simon-Thirring proved $N_c/Z\to1$ for atoms, and later work gave sublinear and explicit bounds such as $1.22Z+3Z^{1/3}$, but no uniform bound on the excess. Simon's Problem 9 (2000) asks whether $N_c(Z)-Z$ stays bounded for atoms; the molecular form asks for $N_c\le Z+CM$ with $M$ nuclei (Lewin 2025). The ionization conjecture as surveyed by Solovej also asks that the first ionization energy and the outer radius of neutral atoms stay bounded independently of $Z$. Is the excess charge bounded by a universal constant per nucleus, and are the neutral-atom ionization energy and radius bounded uniformly in $Z$?

fields.name: Solovej's generalized ionization conjecture for neutral Coulomb atoms (energies and radii)
fields.statement: For the full nonrelativistic Coulomb atom with nuclear charge $Z$ and two spin states, let $I_m(Z)=E_Z(Z-m)-E_Z(Z)$ be the energy needed to remove $m$ electrons from the neutral atom, and let $R_m(Z)$ be the radius outside which an expected $m$ electrons of a neutral ground state lie. Thomas-Fermi theory predicts $I_m^{TF}\sim a_{TF}m^{7/3}$ and radii $\sim(81\pi^2/2)^{1/3}m^{-1/3}$ as $Z\to\infty$ and then $m\to\infty$. Solovej (2016) conjectured that the same asymptotics hold for the true many-body atom: $\lim_{m\to\infty}m^{-7/3}\limsup_{Z\to\infty}I_m(Z)=\lim_{m\to\infty}m^{-7/3}\liminf_{Z\to\infty}I_m(Z)=a_{TF}$, and likewise $m^{1/3}R_m(Z)\to(81\pi^2/2)^{1/3}$ for the upper and lower large-$Z$ limits. He had proved the analogues in Hartree-Fock theory. Do these iterated limits hold for the full Schrodinger atom?

fields.statement: In the classical nearest-neighbour $O(n)$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$, spins $\sigma_x\in S^{n-1}$ carry the Gibbs weight $\exp(\beta\sum_{x\sim y}\sigma_x\cdot\sigma_y)$. Mermin and Wagner showed there is no spontaneous magnetization at any $\beta<\infty$, and McBryan-Spencer gave algebraic upper bounds on correlations, but these allow a zero exponential rate. For $n=2$ the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase (Frohlich-Spencer) has only power-law decay at low temperature. For $n\ge3$ Polyakov's renormalization argument (1975) predicts mass generation at every positive temperature; rigorous proofs covered only high temperature (Aizenman-Simon) and large $n$ (Kupiainen). Do two-point correlations $\langle\sigma_x\cdot\sigma_y\rangle$ decay exponentially in $|x-y|$ for every $n\ge3$ and every finite $\beta>0$?
fields.posedBy: Alexander M. Polyakov (Phys. Lett. B 59, 1975), predicting mass generation for n >= 3; recorded as an open conjecture by Aru, Garban and Sepulveda (Comm. Math. Phys., 2025)

fields.field: Constructive quantum field theory; asymptotically free sigma models
fields.statement: The two-dimensional $O(3)$ nonlinear sigma model is the lattice measure $\propto\exp(\beta\sum_{x\sim y}q_x\cdot q_y)\prod_x d\sigma(q_x)$ with $q_x\in S^2$. Perturbative renormalization (Polyakov 1975; Brezin-Zinn-Justin 1976) predicts asymptotic freedom: as $\beta\to\infty$ and the lattice spacing shrinks, a finite physical mass survives, and integrability (Zamolodchikov-Zamolodchikov; Hasenfratz-Maggiore-Niedermayer) describes the expected massive continuum theory. Rigorous constructions existed only for large $N$ (Kupiainen, Kopper), for a hierarchical model (Gawedzki-Kupiainen), or in perturbation theory (Mitter-Ramadas), with Balaban's program partial. Does the nearest-neighbour lattice $O(3)$ model have a continuum limit that satisfies the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms, is interacting (non-Gaussian), and has a positive mass gap?

fields.name: The Bochner-Riesz conjecture in three dimensions (strict-order range)
fields.field: Harmonic analysis; Fourier multipliers and summability
fields.statement: For $\delta\ge0$ the Bochner-Riesz means on $\mathbb R^n$ are $\widehat{T_\delta f}(\xi)=(1-|\xi|^2)_+^\delta\widehat f(\xi)$. Fefferman (1971) showed the ball multiplier ($\delta=0$) is unbounded on $L^p$ for $p\ne2$ when $n\ge2$; Carleson and Sjolin (1972) proved the conjectured range in the plane. The Bochner-Riesz conjecture asserts that $T_\delta$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ whenever $\delta>\max\{n|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\}$; Tao (1999) showed it implies the restriction conjecture. In $\mathbb R^3$ the strict range was known only for $\max\{p,p'\}\ge 22/7$ (Lee, Wu, Gao-Wu-Xi). Is $T_\delta$ bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every $1\le p\le\infty$ and every $\delta>\max\{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\}$?

fields.name: The four-dimensional disc embedding conjecture and whether the free group is good
fields.shortName: Disc embedding conjecture; is F2 good?
fields.statement: Freedman's disc embedding theorem says: in an oriented 4-manifold $M$ with good fundamental group $\pi$, immersed discs $f_i$ with embedded boundaries and framed algebraically dual spheres $g_j$ ($\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0=\widetilde\mu(g_i)$ in $\mathbb Z[\pi]$) can be replaced by disjoint locally flat embedded discs with the same boundary. Does the disc embedding conclusion hold without the good-group hypothesis; in particular, is the free group $F_2$ good?

fields.name: Wall's manifold-realization question for finitely presented Poincare duality groups
fields.field: Geometric group theory; aspherical manifolds and Poincare duality groups
fields.statement: A group $G$ is an integral Poincare duality group of dimension $n$ if $\mathbb Z$ has a finite projective $\mathbb ZG$-resolution and $H^i(G;\mathbb ZG)$ vanishes for $i\ne n$ and is $\mathbb Z$ for $i=n$. fields.name: Dixmier's unitarizability problem for discrete groups
fields.field: Group theory; amenability and uniformly bounded representations
fields.statement: A representation $\pi:G\to GL(H)$ of a discrete group on a Hilbert space is uniformly bounded if $\sup_g\|\pi(g)\|<\infty$, and unitarizable if some bounded invertible $S$ makes every $S\pi(g)S^{-1}$ unitary; $G$ is unitarizable if every uniformly bounded representation is. Day and Dixmier (1950) showed amenable groups are unitarizable, and groups containing a nonabelian free subgroup are not (Ehrenpreis-Mautner, Pytlik-Szwarc). Partial converses were known via Pisier's quantitative criterion, Epstein-Monod, Osin, Monod-Ozawa and Vergara. Dixmier asked whether unitarizability characterizes amenability: is every unitarizable discrete group amenable?

fields.name: The Burger-Ozawa-Thom question: does strong Ulam stability characterize amenability?
fields.field: Group theory; stability of approximate representations
fields.statement: A countable discrete group $G$ is strongly Ulam stable if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that every map $\mu:G\to U(H)$ into the unitary group of any complex Hilbert space, with $\mu(e)=I$ and $\sup_{g,h}\|\mu(gh)-\mu(g)\mu(h)\|\le\delta$, is within $\varepsilon$ uniformly of a genuine unitary representation on the same space. Kazhdan (1982) proved amenable groups are strongly Ulam stable; Burger, Ozawa and Thom (2013) showed groups with a nonabelian free subgroup are not, and Alpeev handled wreath products over nonamenable groups. Burger, Ozawa and Thom asked: is every strongly Ulam stable countable group amenable?

fields.statement: Let $X$ be a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic (hyperkahler) Kahler manifold of dimension $2n$ with Beauville-Bogomolov-Fujiki form $q$. fields.name: The Zariski cancellation problem for complex affine space in dimension four
fields.statement: Zariski's cancellation problem asks whether affine space is determined by its cylinder: if $X$ is an affine variety with $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^{n+1}$, must $X\cong\mathbb A^n$? Algebraically, over $\mathbb C$: if $A$ is a finitely generated complex algebra with $A[w]\cong\mathbb C^{[n+1]}$, is $A\cong\mathbb C^{[n]}$? It holds for $n=1$ (Abhyankar-Eakin-Heinzer) and $n=2$ (Fujita, Miyanishi-Sugie). Gupta (2014) showed it fails for every $n\ge3$ in positive characteristic, and the characteristic-zero case in dimensions $n\ge3$ is listed as open in Gaifullin-Petrov (July 2026) and Gupta's ICM 2022 survey. Does cancellation hold for complex affine space in dimension $n\ge3$, in particular for $n=4$?
fields.posedBy: Oscar Zariski; the manuscript cites Abhyankar-Eakin-Heinzer (1972), Fujita (1979), Gupta's ICM 2022 survey and Gaifullin-Petrov (2026) for the problem and its status
fields.ageNote: The manuscript gives no date for the posing. fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: with $P=\mathbb C[p,s,u,F,J]$, $x=s^2+u^3+p^2F$ and $H=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu$, the algebra $A=P/(H)$ is an integral complex domain of dimension four with $A[w]\cong\mathbb C^{[5]}$ but $A\not\cong\mathbb C^{[4]}$. The stabilization uses that $H$ is a residual coordinate (El Kahoui-Ouali, Dutta-Lahiri); non-polynomiality is proved by degenerating to a graded algebra, lifting a putative additive action through a torus bundle over a quadric, and excluding it by a Mason-Stothers abc argument. It answers only $n=4$: dimension three is not treated, and the paper notes that adjoining variables to a counterexample does not by itself give counterexamples in higher dimensions.

fields.name: The Dolgachev-Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture
fields.statement: An $\mathbb A^r$-fibration is a morphism whose fiber over every point is affine $r$-space over the residue field. Dolgachev and Weisfeiler (1974, Section 3.8.5) predicted that an affine morphism to a normal, locally noetherian, integral base all of whose fibers are $\mathbb A^r$ over their residue fields is Zariski-locally trivial, that is, locally a product with $\mathbb A^r$. Is every such affine-space fibration over a normal integral base, for instance over $\mathbb A^1$ or $\mathbb A^2$ over $\mathbb C$, a Zariski-locally trivial $\mathbb A^r$-bundle?
fields.posedBy: B. Yu. Weisfeiler and I. V. Dolgachev, Unipotent group schemes over integral rings, Math. USSR-Izv. 8 (1974), Section 3.8.5
fields.resultNote: Corollary 7.1: for the fourfold $X=\mathrm{Spec}\,A$ of the cancellation counterexample, the maps $\pi:X\to\mathbb A^1$ (given by $p$) and $\rho=(p,H):\mathbb A^5\to\mathbb A^2$ are smooth surjective morphisms of relative dimension three whose fiber over every point is $\mathbb A^3$ over the residue field, yet neither is Zariski-locally trivial. Local triviality would make $A$ a locally polynomial algebra over $\mathbb C[p]$ and hence, by Bass-Connell-Wright and Quillen-Suslin, a polynomial ring, contradicting Theorem 1.1. So the conjecture fails in relative dimension three over the smooth bases $\mathbb A^1$ and $\mathbb A^2$. Relative dimension two is not addressed.

fields.name: The K(pi,1) conjecture for Artin groups of finite rank
fields.statement: For a Coxeter matrix $M$ on a finite set $S$, the Artin group $A_M$ is the fundamental group of the quotient of the complexified hyperplane complement of the Coxeter group $W$ by $W$, and of the finite Salvetti complex $X(W,S)$, which has one cell per spherical subset of $S$. Deligne (1972) proved asphericity when $W$ is finite; Charney-Davis proved the FC and dimension-two cases, Paolini-Salvetti the affine case, Huang-Przytycki dimension three. The $K(\pi,1)$ conjecture, attributed to Arnol'd, Brieskorn, Pham and Thom and listed as Problem 1 in Charney's Artin-group problem list, asserts asphericity in general. Is the Salvetti complex (equivalently the hyperplane-complement quotient) a $K(A_M,1)$ for every Coxeter matrix?
fields.posedBy: Attributed to Arnol'd, Brieskorn, Pham and Thom; stated in Brieskorn's Bourbaki seminar (LNM 317, 1973); Problem 1 in R. Charney, Problems related to Artin groups

fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every Coxeter matrix on a finite set, with arbitrary finite or infinite labels and connected or disconnected diagrams, the universal cover of the full Salvetti complex $X(W,S)$ is contractible, so $\pi_n(X)=0$ for $n\ge2$. The proof contracts the poset of spherical cosets by a well-ordered vertex filtration, using a framed zigzag-algebra braid action whose layer multiplicities define a harmonic height. fields.name: The CAT(0) conjecture for Artin groups
fields.statement: Charney asked which Artin groups are CAT(0) groups (Problem 4 in her Artin-group problem list), and the affirmative expectation that every finite-rank Artin group acts geometrically, that is properly, cocompactly and by isometries, on a proper CAT(0) space is recorded by Haettel (2022) as Conjecture 1.1. It is known for right-angled Artin groups, three-generator large-type groups (Brady-McCammond), XXL type (Haettel) and braid groups on up to seven strands. Does every finite-rank Artin group admit a geometric action on a proper CAT(0) space?

fields.name: The Parabolic Intersection Conjecture for Artin groups
fields.statement: A parabolic subgroup of an Artin group $A_M$ is a conjugate $gA_Xg^{-1}$ of a standard subgroup generated by a subset $X$ of the generators. The Parabolic Intersection Conjecture, formulated precisely in Godelle (2023, Conjecture 1) and Cumplido's survey (Conjecture 4), asserts that the intersection of two parabolic subgroups is parabolic. It was known for right-angled, spherical (Cumplido-Gebhardt-Gonzalez-Meneses-Wiest), large-type, some two-dimensional and some affine and FC types. Is the intersection of any two parabolic subgroups of an arbitrary finite-rank Artin group again parabolic?

The proof uses a relative harmonic height for a framed zigzag braid action and does not use asphericity of the Salvetti complex.

fields.name: The word problem for finite-rank Artin groups
fields.statement: An Artin group is given by generators $\sigma_s$, $s\in S$, and braid relations equating the alternating words of length $m_{st}$ in $\sigma_s,\sigma_t$. Garside, Brieskorn-Saito and Deligne solved the word problem for spherical (finite-type) Artin groups, and it is known for further classes such as large type (Holt-Rees) and diagrams without $A_3$ or $B_3$ subdiagrams (Blasco-Garcia et al. 2026), but no algorithm was known in general. Charney's problem list asks (Problem 10) for solvable word and conjugacy problems in infinite type, and Blasco-Garcia, Cumplido, Holt, Morris-Wright and Rees pose the general decidability question explicitly. Is the word problem decidable for every Artin group with finitely many generators?
fields.posedBy: R. Charney, Problems related to Artin groups, Problem 10 (word and conjugacy problems); posed explicitly in Blasco-Garcia, Cumplido, Holt, Morris-Wright and Rees, J. Algebra 703 (2026)
fields.ageNote: Charney's problem list is undated in the family's references, and the 2026 paper restates a long-standing question; the manuscripts give no original date. Charney's Problem 10 also asks for the conjugacy problem, which is not addressed.
fields.resultNote: Corollary 1.3 of the parabolic-intersections manuscript: there is an algorithm that, given a finite Coxeter matrix $M$, a subset $X$ and words $u,v$, decides whether $v\in uA_Xu^{-1}$; with $X=\varnothing$ this decides the word problem for every finite-rank Artin group. The algorithm uses the framed zigzag-algebra action, shown faithful in Section 8, computed exactly over a cyclotomic field, and tests one transported projective by Gaussian elimination. No complexity bound is asserted, and the conjugacy problem is not treated.

fields.name: Deterministic polynomial-time factorization of polynomials over prime fields
fields.statement: Berlekamp's algorithms (1967, 1970) reduce factoring $f\in\mathbb F_p[x]$ to finding separating elements of a quotient algebra, and randomized algorithms such as Cantor-Zassenhaus factor in expected time polynomial in $\deg f$ and $\log p$. Deterministically, Shoup's bound depends on $p^{1/2+o(1)}$; under GRH, Ronyai handled a bounded number of factors and Evdokimov obtained $(n^{\log n}\log p)^{O(1)}$, still quasipolynomial. Altman (2025) surveys the remaining obstacles. Is there a deterministic algorithm that completely factors every polynomial of degree $n$ over $\mathbb F_p$, with $p$ given in binary, in time polynomial in $n$ and $\log p$, without GRH?
fields.posedBy: Long-standing problem in the line of Berlekamp (1967, 1970); the manuscript cites Altman, arXiv:2509.12705 (2025), for a recent account and names no original poser
fields.ageNote: The manuscript traces the setting to Berlekamp's 1967 and 1970 papers and the deterministic results of Ronyai (1988), Shoup (1990) and Evdokimov (1994), but does not say who first posed the deterministic question or when.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: a uniform deterministic algorithm computes the complete factorization (irreducible factors with multiplicities) of any nonzero dense $f\in\mathbb F_p[x]$ in $O(((n+1)\lceil\log_2 p\rceil)^{10^{12}})$ bit operations, with no randomness, oracle or GRH. Theorem 1.2 (proved here, unconditional) does this given small auxiliary primes $\ell\equiv1\pmod{12q}$ with $p$ not a $q$th power mod $\ell$; the odd-degree splitter uses Jacobians of cyclic curves $Y^q=F(X)$ and norm equations in cyclic algebras. Small auxiliary primes are deduced from a uniform zero-free strip $\mathrm{Re}\,s>1-10^{-6}$ for all finite-order Hecke L-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $\mu_{12}$, imported from the companion on primitive roots and not proved here. The exponent is not practical.

fields.name: Yau's uniformization conjecture
fields.statement: In his 1982 problem survey Yau asked whether a complete noncompact Kahler manifold with positive holomorphic bisectional curvature must be biholomorphic to $\mathbb C^n$, a noncompact counterpart of the Frankel conjecture (settled by Mori and Siu-Yau). It was known under extra hypotheses: maximal volume growth (Chau-Tam, Liu, Lee-Tam), curvature decay or pinching, and recently for surfaces with positive sectional curvature (Datar-Pingali-Seshadri). Is every complete connected noncompact Kahler manifold of complex dimension $n$ with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature biholomorphic to $\mathbb C^n$?
fields.posedBy: S.-T. Yau, Survey on partial differential equations in differential geometry, Seminar on Differential Geometry, Ann. of Math. Stud. 102 (1982), Section 9(b), p. 45
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: if a connected noncompact complex manifold of dimension $n\ge1$ carries a smooth complete Kahler metric with pointwise strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature, then it is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C^n$; no curvature bounds, volume growth, noncollapsing or topological hypotheses are assumed. The proof runs a Kahler-Ricci flow built from exhaustions, proves Harnack inequalities by a disc-minimization argument, obtains shrinking holomorphic charts and assembles them by polynomial-automorphism dynamics into a biholomorphism onto all of $\mathbb C^n$. It does not say the metric is flat, and it does not treat nonnegative curvature.

fields.name: The hyperinvariant subspace problem on Hilbert space
fields.statement: A closed subspace is hyperinvariant for a bounded operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $H$ if it is invariant under every operator commuting with $T$; equivalently, $T$ has no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace exactly when its commutant $\{T\}'$ is a transitive algebra. Douglas and Pearcy (1972) studied the problem and its link to transitive algebras; it sits beside the invariant subspace problem and is known to be distinct from it (a claimed equivalence by Kerchy-Pearcy was withdrawn). Does every bounded nonscalar operator on an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space have a nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace?
fields.posedBy: Classical operator-theory problem; the manuscript cites R. G. Douglas and C. Pearcy, Hyperinvariant subspaces and transitive algebras, Michigan Math. J. 19 (1972), and names no original poser
fields.ageNote: The earliest source the manuscripts cite for the problem is Douglas-Pearcy (1972), described as studying it rather than posing it; no posing date is given.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2: on $L^2(\mathbb Z_2;\ell^2(\mathbb Z))$ a fibered bilateral weighted shift $S$ with quadratically decaying weights over the 2-adic odometer is nonzero with $\|S^n\|\le\exp(-10\lfloor(n+1)^2/4\rfloor)$, hence norm-quasinilpotent, and its commutant (containing a backward intertwiner $V$ and all scalar multipliers) is transitive. So every infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space carries a nonzero quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace. The operator has many ordinary invariant subspaces (the fiberwise tails), so the invariant subspace problem itself is untouched. The companion reaches the same existence statement by a different construction.

fields.name: The transitive algebra problem
fields.statement: An algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space $H$ is transitive if its only common closed invariant subspaces are $\{0\}$ and $H$. Arveson (1967) proved that a transitive algebra containing a maximal abelian self-adjoint algebra is strongly dense in $B(H)$, and Douglas and Pearcy (1972) related the general question to hyperinvariant subspaces. Is every unital transitive operator algebra on an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space strongly (equivalently weakly) dense in $B(H)$?
fields.posedBy: Question in the setting of W. B. Arveson, A density theorem for operator algebras, Duke Math. J. 34 (1967); the manuscript states it without attribution
fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Arveson (1967) for the main positive result and Douglas-Pearcy (1972) for the link to hyperinvariant subspaces, but does not say who posed the question or when; the conventional attribution to Arveson 1967 is not made in the source.
fields.resultNote: Corollary 1.2 of the principal manuscript: the commutant of the constructed nonzero quasinilpotent operator $S$ is a proper, strongly closed, unital, transitive complex algebra, so it is not strongly dense in $B(H)$. This answers the question negatively on every infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. It is an immediate consequence of the hyperinvariant counterexample, since the commutant of an operator without hyperinvariant subspaces is transitive. The algebra is a commutant, so nothing is said about singly generated transitive algebras, which is the invariant subspace problem.

fields.name: Zhu, Fang and Shi's question on invariant projections of weighted irrational rotations
fields.statement: For irrational $\theta$, let $R_\theta$ be the hyperfinite II$_1$ factor generated by unitaries $U,V$ with $VU=e^{2\pi i\theta}UV$, and for $f$ on the circle let $T_f=Uf(V)$. Haagerup-Schultz give nontrivial invariant projections in the factor whenever the Brown measure is not a point mass; for these operators that happens exactly when the Fuglede-Kadison determinant $\exp\int\log|f|\,dm$ is positive. Zhu, Fang and Shi (2017, p. 264) asked: if $f$ is nonzero almost everywhere, $|f|$ is nonconstant and the determinant is zero, must $T_f$ have a nontrivial invariant projection $p\in R_\theta$, that is, $0<\tau(p)<1$ and $(1-p)T_fp=0$?
fields.posedBy: Z. Zhu, J. Fang and R. Shi, On a class of operators in the hyperfinite II1 factor, Math. Scand. (2017), p. 264, question after Proposition 5.7
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for every irrational $\theta\in(0,1)$ there is a continuous $f:\mathbb T\to[0,1]$ vanishing only at $1$, with $\int\log f\,dm=-\infty$, such that every projection $p\in R_\theta$ with $(1-p)Uf(V)p=0$ is $0$ or $1$; the operator is nonzero and norm-quasinilpotent. The angle is prescribed in advance with no Diophantine condition. Invariant subspaces of the Hilbert-space representation whose projections lie outside the factor are not excluded. An appendix gives a second realization on an infinite product of circles.

fields.name: Irrationality of Catalan's constant
fields.statement: Catalan's constant is $G=\beta(2)=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2=L(2,\chi_{-4})$, the simplest even value of the Dirichlet beta function. Odd beta values are rational multiples of powers of $\pi$, but nothing was known about the arithmetic of $G$ itself. Rivoal and Zudilin (2003) proved that infinitely many even beta values are irrational and that at least one of $\beta(2),\beta(4),\ldots,\beta(14)$ is, a list later cut to $\beta(2),\ldots,\beta(10)$; such family results never single out $G$. Apery-like recurrences and continued fractions for $G$ (Zudilin 2003) converge fast, but the integer linear forms they give do not tend to zero once denominators are cleared. Is Catalan's constant irrational?

fields.name: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for a single transformation
fields.statement: Let $T$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation of a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)$. $T$ is mixing if $\mu(A\cap T^{-n}B)\to\mu(A)\mu(B)$ as $|n|\to\infty$, and mixing of order $k$ if $\mu(\bigcap_{i=1}^k T^{-t_i}A_i)\to\prod_i\mu(A_i)$ whenever $t_1<\cdots<t_k$ and $\min_i(t_{i+1}-t_i)\to\infty$. Rokhlin introduced higher-order mixing in 1949 and asked whether ordinary mixing already implies mixing of the next order. Partial answers needed extra structure: Kalikow (rank one, threefold), Host (singular spectrum), Ryzhikov (finite rank), while Ledrappier's mixing $\mathbb Z^2$ action that is not threefold mixing shows the question is specific to one transformation. fields.statement: Let $Q$ be a closed connected smooth manifold and $T^*Q$ its cotangent bundle with the canonical symplectic form. fields.name: Kaplansky's quasitrace problem: is every 2-quasitrace on a unital C*-algebra a trace?
fields.field: Operator algebras; traces and quasitraces on C*-algebras
fields.statement: A 1-quasitrace on a unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ is a function $\tau:A\to\mathbb C$ with $\tau(x^*x)=\tau(xx^*)\ge0$, $\tau(h+ik)=\tau(h)+i\tau(k)$ for self-adjoint $h,k$, and linear on every abelian $C^*$-subalgebra; it is a 2-quasitrace if it extends to such a function on $M_2(A)$. Blackadar and Handelman showed 2-quasitraces correspond to dimension functions, and the question whether every one is linear is equivalent to Kaplansky's 1951 question whether every $AW^*$-factor of type II$_1$ is a von Neumann algebra. Haagerup proved it for exact algebras, and Milhoj and Rordam showed it is equivalent to asking whether the minimal tensor product of two unital simple stably finite $C^*$-algebras is stably finite. Is every normalized 2-quasitrace on every unital $C^*$-algebra a tracial state?

fields.ageNote: The manuscript dates Kaplansky's introduction of AW*-algebras to 1951 through Gow's 2026 account and treats the factor question and the quasitrace problem as equivalent (Milhoj-Rordam Section 2, Gow Theorem 4.11). The quasitrace formulation dates from Blackadar and Handelman (1982); the manuscript does not cite Kaplansky's own paper.

fields.name: The Falconer distance conjecture
fields.statement: For $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ let $\Delta(E)=\{|x-y|:x,y\in E\}$ be its distance set. Falconer (1985) showed that $\dim_H E>(d+1)/2$ forces $\Delta(E)$ to have positive Lebesgue measure, and lattice-type examples show the threshold cannot go below $d/2$. Later thresholds were $4/3$ in the plane (Wolff), $d/2+1/3$ (Erdogan), $9/5$ in $\mathbb R^3$ and further improvements via decoupling (Du, Guth, Ou, Wang, Wilson, Zhang; Du, Zhang), and $5/4$ in the plane for pinned distances (Guth, Iosevich, Ou, Wang). fields.name: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2
fields.statement: The irrationality exponent of an irrational $x$ is $\mu(x)=\sup\{\nu>0: 0<|x-p/q|<q^{-\nu}$ for infinitely many coprime $p,q$, $q\ge2\}$; Dirichlet's pigeonhole argument gives $\mu(x)\ge2$, and almost every real has $\mu=2$. fields.name: Sinai's conjecture: positive metric entropy of the standard map for a positive-measure set of parameters
fields.statement: The standard map $f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k\sin(2\pi x),\,y+k\sin(2\pi x))$ on $\mathbb T^2$ preserves area $m$ and was introduced by Chirikov as a model of conservative chaos. For large $k$ it has hyperbolic sets (Duarte), full-dimension transitive sets for residual parameters (Gorodetski) and positive topological entropy (Oliveira), but also elliptic islands, and none of this gives positive area. Sinai's conjecture, in the formulation of Berger and Turaev (2019, Conjecture 0.4), asks: is the metric entropy $h_m(f_k)$, equivalently a positive Lyapunov exponent on positive area, positive for a set of parameters $k$ of positive Lebesgue measure?

fields.name: Infinitely many closed geodesics on every Riemannian sphere and every closed three-manifold
fields.statement: The closed-geodesic infinitude problem asks whether every closed Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two has infinitely many geometrically distinct (distinct image) closed geodesics. fields.name: The generator problem: is every von Neumann algebra with separable predual singly generated?

fields.name: The Lipschitz isomorphism problem for separable Banach spaces
fields.statement: Banach spaces $X,Y$ are Lipschitz isomorphic if there is a bijection $\Psi:X\to Y$ with $c\|s-t\|\le\|\Psi s-\Psi t\|\le C\|s-t\|$ for constants $0<c\le C$. Kalton listed the question as Problem 3 in his 2008 survey. Must two separable Banach spaces that are Lipschitz isomorphic be linearly isomorphic?

fields.name: The matrix multiplication exponent: is omega at most 9/4?
fields.field: Algebraic complexity, bilinear and tensor methods
fields.statement: The exponent $\omega$ of matrix multiplication over $\mathbb C$ is the infimum of the $\tau$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, two $n\times n$ matrices can be multiplied with $O_\varepsilon(n^{\tau+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic operations. Strassen's 1969 algorithm gave $\omega\le\log_2 7<2.81$, and the laser method of Strassen, Coppersmith-Winograd and their successors (Stothers, Vassilevska Williams, Le Gall, Alman-Vassilevska Williams, Duan-Wu-Zhou and others) brought the bound down to $\omega<2.371177$ (Dupont et al., 2026). The trivial lower bound is $\omega\ge2$, and whether $\omega=2$ is a central open question of algebraic complexity. The related dual exponent $\alpha$, the largest $k$ for which $n\times n^k$ by $n^k\times n$ products take $n^{2+o(1)}$ operations, was known to satisfy $\alpha\ge0.321334$. How small can the upper bound on $\omega$ be made?

fields.name: The forcing conjecture for bipartite graphs

fields.statement: Let $W\subset\mathbb C$ be a simply connected domain whose boundary in the Riemann sphere has at least two points, and $\varphi:W\to\mathbb D$ a conformal bijection onto the unit disk. fields.name: Local smooth isometric immersion of surfaces in three-space
fields.shortName: Local isometric immersion of smooth surfaces in R3
fields.statement: Given a smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on a surface, can a neighbourhood of each point be realised as a smooth surface in $\mathbb R^3$, i.e. is there a smooth $F$ with $\langle\partial_iF,\partial_jF\rangle=g_{ij}$ near the point? fields.name: A fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in general graphs
fields.shortName: FPRAS for perfect matchings in general graphs
fields.field: Approximate counting; Markov chain Monte Carlo
fields.statement: Counting perfect matchings exactly is #P-complete even for bipartite graphs (Valiant 1979). fields.name: The Hadwiger-Nelson problem: the Euclidean plane is not five-colorable
fields.field: Euclidean Ramsey theory; chromatic number of the plane
fields.statement: Color every point of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ so that any two points at distance exactly $1$ receive different colors, with no regularity imposed on the color classes. fields.name: Zariski's multiplicity conjecture: does embedded topology determine the multiplicity of a hypersurface singularity?
fields.field: Singularity theory; topology of hypersurface singularities
fields.statement: For a reduced convergent power series $f\in\mathbb{C}\{z_1,\ldots,z_N\}$ with $f(0)=0$, the multiplicity of the hypersurface germ $V(f)$ is $\mathrm{ord}_0 f$, the least degree of a monomial in $f$. fields.name: Ryser's conjecture on covers of r-partite hypergraphs
fields.field: Extremal hypergraph theory; covers and matchings
fields.statement:
An $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ has disjoint vertex parts $V_1,\ldots,V_r$ and every edge has exactly one vertex in each part. Let $	au(H)$ be its covering number (least size of a vertex set meeting every edge) and $
u(H)$ its matching number. Ryser's conjecture asserts $	au(H)\le(r-1)
u(H)$. For $r=2$ this is Konig's theorem; Aharoni proved $r=3$; in the intersecting case ($
u=1$) it was known through $r=5$ (Gyarfas, Tuza), and truncated projective planes show it would be tight whenever $r-1$ is a prime power. Does every $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph satisfy $	au(H)\le(r-1)
u(H)$?

fields.name: Gyarfas's conjecture on covering edge-colored complete graphs by r-1 monochromatic trees
fields.statement: Color each edge of a finite complete graph with one of $r$ colors. A monochromatic tree cover is a family of monochromatic trees (overlaps and single vertices allowed) whose vertex sets cover the graph. fields.name: The two-point Chowla conjecture (ordinary averages)
fields.field: Analytic number theory; correlations of multiplicative functions
fields.statement: Let $\lambda(n)=(-1)^{\Omega(n)}$ be the Liouville function. Chowla's conjecture predicts that $\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n+h_1)\cdots\lambda(n+h_k)=o(X)$ for every fixed set of distinct shifts. Its two-point case asks whether the parities of $\Omega(n)$ and $\Omega(n+h)$ become uncorrelated. Matomaki and Radziwill obtained a bound $(1-\delta(h))X$, Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao proved cancellation on average over shifts, and Tao proved the logarithmically averaged version, with quantitative log-averaged savings by Helfgott-Radziwill and Pilatte. Does $\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n)\lambda(n+h)=o(X)$ hold for every fixed $h\ge1$?

fields.name: The binary corrected Elliott conjecture for ordinary averages
fields.field: Analytic number theory; pretentious multiplicative functions
fields.statement: Elliott (1992) conjectured that correlations $\frac1N\sum_{n\le N}f_1(n+h_1)\cdots f_k(n+h_k)$ of multiplicative functions bounded by one tend to zero when one factor does not pretend to be a twisted character. Matomaki, Radziwill and Tao showed the original hypothesis is insufficient for complex functions and corrected it: with $D(f,\chi n^{it};N)^2=\sum_{p\le N}(1-\mathrm{Re}\,f(p)\overline{\chi(p)}p^{-it})/p$, require $\inf_{|t|\le N}D(f,\chi n^{it};N)\to\infty$ for every fixed Dirichlet character $\chi$. Tao proved the logarithmically averaged binary case, and Tao-Teravainen and Klurman-Mangerel-Teravainen proved it along most scales. For multiplicative $f_1,f_2:\mathbb{N}\to\{|z|\le1\}$ with one factor uniformly nonpretentious and fixed distinct $h_1,h_2$, does $\frac1N\sum_{n\le N}f_1(n+h_1)f_2(n+h_2)\to0$?

fields.name: The Benjamini-Schramm criticality conjecture for bond percolation on quasi-transitive graphs
fields.field: Percolation theory on graphs and groups
fields.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite, connected, locally finite quasi-transitive graph (its automorphism group has finitely many vertex orbits) and run Bernoulli percolation on $G$ with critical probability $p_c<1$. Benjamini and Schramm (1996, Conjecture 4) conjectured that critical percolation dies on every such graph: at $p=p_c$ there is almost surely no infinite open cluster. Their paper discusses site percolation and says the questions remain equally valid for bond percolation outside planar settings. The motivating case is $\mathbb Z^d$, where $\theta(p_c)=0$ was known for $d=2$ and in high dimensions only. Does critical Bernoulli bond percolation have no infinite cluster on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with $p_c<1$?
fields.posedBy: Itai Benjamini and Oded Schramm, Percolation beyond Z^d, many questions and a few answers (1996), Conjecture 4
fields.ageNote: The $\mathbb Z^d$ special case is older: Benjamini and Schramm call it one of the outstanding challenges of percolation theory, and the catalog entry for it dates it to Kesten (1982). Benjamini and Schramm state their conjectures for site percolation and say they carry over to bond percolation; this entry is the bond form.

Both manuscripts are credited to OpenAI with no human author named. The quasi-transitive manuscript credits earlier public AI-produced work on the Kozma-Nitzan gluing inequality (Leder's Lean account for Z^d, and expositions prompted by Ahmed Bou-Rabee) and gives its own proof of the gluing input.

fields.name: Koebe's circle-domain conjecture (Kreisnormierungsproblem)
fields.statement: A circle domain is a domain in the Riemann sphere $\hat{\mathbb C}$ each of whose complementary components is a closed round disk or a single point. Koebe proved that every finitely connected domain is conformally equivalent to a circle domain, and He and Schramm (1993) extended this to countably connected domains. Koebe's Kreisnormierungsproblem, posed in 1908, asks for the general case, with no restriction on the number or shape of the complementary components, which may be uncountably many. Is every domain $G\subseteq\hat{\mathbb C}$ conformally equivalent to a circle domain?

The manuscript is credited to OpenAI with no human author named.

fields.name: He-Schramm rigidity conjecture: circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid
fields.field: Geometric function theory; conformal rigidity and removability
fields.statement: A circle domain $\Omega\subseteq\hat{\mathbb C}$ is conformally rigid if every conformal equivalence from $\Omega$ onto another circle domain is the restriction of a Mobius transformation. A compact set $E$ is conformally removable if every orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the sphere that is conformal off $E$ is Mobius. He and Schramm proved rigidity for countably connected circle domains and for boundaries of $\sigma$-finite length, and conjectured that a circle domain is rigid if and only if its boundary is conformally removable. Rajala (2025) disproved the rigid-implies-removable direction. Is every circle domain whose boundary is conformally removable conformally rigid?

fields.name: The Haldane gap conjecture for the spin-one Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain
fields.statement: For the spin-one antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain $H_L=\sum_j \mathbf S_j\cdot\mathbf S_{j+1}$ with spin-one matrices normalized by $\sum_\alpha (S^\alpha)^2=2$, Haldane predicted in 1981 (published 1983) that integer-spin chains, unlike half-odd-integer ones, have a unique ground state separated from the rest of the spectrum by a gap that stays positive in the thermodynamic limit. AKLT proved such a gap for a modified model with a biquadratic term, Yarotsky for small perturbations of it, and numerics put the Heisenberg gap near $0.41$, but no proof existed for the pure bilinear model. fields.name: The Harary-Hill conjecture on the crossing number of complete graphs
fields.statement: The crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G)$ is the least number of crossing points in a drawing of $G$ in the plane, with vertices at distinct points and edges as simple arcs meeting in finitely many proper crossings. It was verified only for $n\le12$ (and reported for $n\le14$), for restricted drawing classes, and asymptotically up to a factor of about $0.986$. Is $\mathrm{cr}(K_n)=Z(n)$ for every $n$?

fields.name: Zarankiewicz's crossing-number conjecture (Turan's brick factory problem)
fields.statement: Turan's brick factory problem (1944) asks for the least number of crossings in a plane drawing of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$, crossings counted as points with edges drawn as simple arcs. fields.name: The Zilber-Pink conjecture for abelian varieties over number fields
fields.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field and $X\subseteq A_{\bar{\mathbb Q}}$ an irreducible subvariety, and let $S$ be the smallest torsion coset containing $X$. A component $Y$ of $X\cap T$, for a torsion coset $T\subseteq S$, is atypical if $\dim Y>\dim X+\dim T-\dim S$. Zilber (2002, for semiabelian varieties) and Pink (2005) conjectured that such unlikely intersections are controlled, generalizing Manin-Mumford and Mordell-Lang. The curve case was proved by Habegger and Pila (2016); higher dimensions were known only under extra quotient-dimension or height conditions or in codimension one or two. Does every such $X$ have only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties?

fields.name: Zilber-Pink for Hodge-generic curves in the Siegel modular threefold A_2
fields.statement: Let $\mathcal A_2$ be the moduli space of principally polarized abelian surfaces. Pink's Zilber-Pink conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties (2005, Conjecture 1.3) predicts that a Hodge-generic curve meets the union of special subvarieties of codimension at least two only finitely often; in $\mathcal A_2$ these are the special points and the special curves (products with a CM elliptic factor, squares of non-CM elliptic curves, quaternionic multiplication). Pila and Tsimerman proved Andre-Oort for $\mathcal A_2$, and Daw and Orr proved the curve loci under boundary or multiplicative-reduction hypotheses. For a Hodge-generic algebraic curve $C\subset\mathcal A_2$ over $\bar{\mathbb Q}$, is $C\cap\bigcup_{\dim Z\le1}Z$ finite?
